{"summary": "Implemented get_Inv_Count using merge-sort inversion counting (O(n log n), non-mutating, respecting n) and added tests covering the example and edge cases.", "files": {"solution.py": """"Write a python function to count inversions in an array."""


def get_Inv_Count(arr, n):
    """Write a python function to count inversions in an array.

    An inversion is a pair of indices ``(i, j)`` with ``i < j`` and
    ``arr[i] > arr[j]``. Only the first ``n`` elements of ``arr`` are
    considered. The input array is not modified.
    """
    if arr is None:
        return 0
    if n is None:
        values = list(arr)
    else:
        values = list(arr[: max(0, n)])

    def merge_count(items):
        if len(items) <= 1:
            return items, 0
        mid = len(items) // 2
        left, left_count = merge_count(items[:mid])
        right, right_count = merge_count(items[mid:])
        merged = []
        split_count = 0
        i = 0
        j = 0
        while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
            if left[i] <= right[j]:
                merged.append(left[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(right[j])
                split_count += len(left) - i
                j += 1
        merged.extend(left[i:])
        merged.extend(right[j:])
        return merged, left_count + right_count + split_count

    _, count = merge_count(values)
    return count
